page: Vultr vx1-m-4c-32g-240s is a memory-optimized virtual server belonging to the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical AMD EPYC cores with 2 threads per core, operating at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The processor includes 32 MB of L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512, including VNNI and BF16 extensions, alongside SHA-ni cryptography. This hardware configuration is bundled with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding 8.0 GB of RAM per core, and 240 GB of local NVMe SSD storage.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong single-core capabilities, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the top 25%. Text processing is a notable strength, ranking in the top 10% of tested systems. Multi-core performance, memory bandwidth, and database operations generally align with the middle 50% average. However, multi-threaded decompression and software compilation tasks exhibit weaker relative performance, falling into the bottom 25%. Large-model LLM prompt processing is also limited, registering in the bottom 10% for 7B models.

This server offers a high memory-to-vCPU density, making it a qualitatively cost-efficient option for memory-bound workloads that do not require massive parallel compute scaling. The primary tradeoff is the lower multi-threaded scaling and modest 2.0 GHz clock speed, which limits its effectiveness for heavy compilation or dense multi-threaded calculations. It is best suited for memory-intensive applications, caching layers, text processing pipelines, lightweight database hosting, and static web serving.
